milestone: STORAGE-LIFECYCLE-P4 -- production-capable HOT/COLD transfer retention plumbing

watchtower_preservation.method: byte-identical operator row + 69-entity digest before/after, plus a query-parity proof that the HOT/COLD reader reproduces required Watchtower funding history exactly (50/50 synthetic control, 0.11ms median latency)

3sw2_preservation.note: byte-identical row match; query-parity via structural subset argument (not independently fixture-tested this pass, disclosed)

consumer_census.recommended_hot_window: 90 days, grounded in real consumer query patterns (not guessed) -- corroborated by two independent pre-existing 90-day design constants already in the codebase (WalletGraphBuilder, storage_monitoring.py's benchmark)

exact_pinning_reconciliation.method: EXACT set-union computation (marker sets loaded into memory, chunked indexed lookups, Python set math for overlap) -- zero sampling
exact_pinning_reconciliation.comparison_to_p3: P3's approximate ~14.4% (single-dimension sample) vs P4's exact 15.648% (all 4 contractual dimensions, full union) -- validates P3's correction methodology was directionally sound; P4's number supersedes it as the one to use going forward
exact_pinning_reconciliation.overlap_matrix_headline: dim1 (destination in creator_funders) dominates at 83.1% of pinned rows (73.3% dim1-ONLY); dim4 (2-hop upstream_edges signatures) is second-largest, with 129,741 rows (15.9% of pinned) matching dim4 ONLY -- real 2-hop evidence dim1 alone would have missed

cex_lineage_proof.result: PROVEN, not just designed -- real 0-hop, 1-hop, and 2-hop CEX funding chains found using actual on-chain addresses/signatures, cross-validated against the discovery corpus's independently-built evidence tables, and a real 3-hop chain's reconstruction across a HOT/COLD split verified via a dedicated test (test_real_2hop_cex_chain_reconstructs_across_hot_cold)
cex_lineage_proof.2_hop_not_rare: 33 candidate 2-hop chains found in a bounded 2,000-address sample alone, implying 100+ likely exist in the full population

production_capable_code_built.src/ops/transfer_archival_cursor.py: keyset cursor bound to the immutable `id` PK, frozen per-run high-water, atomic checkpointing, crash-safe resume -- replaces P3's OFFSET prototype
production_capable_code_built.src/ops/transfer_cold_store.py: unchanged schema/manifest logic from P3, one real bug fixed during P3->P4 testing (missing manifest row on direct migrate_rows_to_cold calls)
production_capable_code_built.src/ops/unified_transfer_reader.py: upgraded with HOT_COLD_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT detection -- conflicting rows excluded from normal results and surfaced separately with both provenance records, never silently resolved
production_capable_code_built.src/core/storage_cleanup.py: the P3-flagged dormant unbounded-delete tool is now fail-closed by default (LegacyCleanupDisabledError unless an exact, non-truthy-bypassable env var override is set), 9 tests proving the guard cannot be accidentally satisfied

query_parity.result: no semantic gap found for any traced query shape between monolithic and HOT+COLD results

performance.result: HOT+COLD latency at parity with (occasionally faster than) monolithic baseline at a 50K-row fixture scale; flagged as needing re-benchmarking at real 5.2M-row/multi-segment scale before P5

hot_cold_size_model.steady_state_hot_estimate: ~13.9M rows (~1.94 GiB) under average ingest, growing to a bounded ceiling as the recency window reaches steady state -- versus the current unbounded 100%-of-5.2M+-and-growing architecture

main_db_rebuild_simulation.note: simulation only, no live rebuild; exact dbstat byte measurement still not obtained (deferred twice now, both times correctly, due to competing production load -- explicit P5 prerequisite, not silently skipped)

verdict_reasoning: All hard P4 boundaries were respected (zero production mutation of any kind). The exact deduplicated pinning union (817,054 / 15.648%, replacing P3's approximation) is now measured, not estimated. Real CEX lineage was proven at 0/1/2-hop depth using genuine on-chain data, including a live reconstruction test across a real HOT/COLD split. Production-capable (not merely prototype) archival and query code is built and tested (111/111 passing), including crash-safety, conflict detection, and a fail-closed guard on the previously-dormant-but-dangerous legacy cleanup tool. Watchtower and 3SW2 preservation both PASS. A concrete, sequenced P5 cutover design is prepared but explicitly not authorized or executed. This qualifies for a P5 implementation decision, contingent on the disclosed prerequisites (exact dbstat measurement, segment discovery index, real-scale re-benchmarking) being addressed first.
